introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné (CamScanner) de 2 pages : page de garde et six questions sur une page ; lu en image, aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food &Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction ; les petites fautes de frappe du sujet (« five(5) », « Bring out five (5) importance of  food and nutrition », « types of food service  . ») sont recopiées telles quelles.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » et les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour les six questions (Q1 : 3+5+6+6+5 ; Q2 : 4+6+10+5 ; Q3 : 10+5+5+5 ; Q4 : 4+6+2+3+5+5 ; Q5 : 2+7+4+6+6 ; Q6 : 5+5+5+5+5) : aucun écart. Les sous-parties (i), (ii) restent dans le texte de la sous-question (d), 4(c), 4(d), 5(a) ou 6(d), dont `points` est la somme imprimée.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées, au nombre exact d'éléments demandé, avec quelques réponses acceptables supplémentaires entre parenthèses. Aucune composition chiffrée de plat ou d'aliment n'est avancée ; les seuls chiffres sont les valeurs énergétiques classiques de la question 3(b), recalculées avec Python.

Question 4(b) : la lumière du soleil est donnée comme première source de vitamine D (source principale, même si ce n'est pas un aliment) ; l'ajout de vitamine D à la margarine « par la loi » est vrai dans plusieurs pays mais n'est pas vérifié pour le Cameroun (l'énoncé du corrigé dit « in many countries »).

Question 4(c)(i) : le rachitisme et l'ostéomalacie sont dus surtout à une carence en vitamine D et en calcium ; ils sont donnés comme réponses attendues, l'ostéoporose, la carie dentaire et la tétanie figurent comme autres réponses acceptables.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State four (4) functions of vitamin D.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four functions of vitamin D (1 mark each):

1. It **helps the body to absorb calcium and phosphorus** from the food in the small intestine.
2. It **helps to build strong bones**, because the calcium and phosphorus are deposited in them (calcification).
3. It **helps to form and harden the teeth.**
4. It **prevents rickets in children and osteomalacia (soft bones) in adults.**

(Another correct answer: it helps to keep the right amount of calcium in the blood.)
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
List six (6) sources of vitamin D.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Six sources of vitamin D (1 mark each):

1. **Sunlight** - the skin makes vitamin D when it is exposed to the sun (the main source, although it is not a food).
2. **Fish liver oils**, for example cod liver oil.
3. **Oily fish**, for example sardines, mackerel, herring or tuna.
4. **Egg yolk.**
5. **Margarine** (vitamin D is added to it by law in many countries).
6. **Liver.**

(Other correct sources, in small amounts: butter, cheese, fortified milk and fortified cereals.)
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
i) State two (2) diseases associated with the deficiency of calcium

(2 marks)

ii) List three (3) advantages of steaming.

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two diseases associated with a lack of calcium (1 mark each)**

1. **Rickets** - in children, the bones are soft and the legs become bent (bow legs).
2. **Osteomalacia** - in adults, the bones become soft and painful and break easily.

(Other acceptable answers: osteoporosis, in which the bones become thin and brittle in old age; tooth decay; tetany, which is painful cramp of the muscles.)

**(ii) Three advantages of steaming (1 mark each)**

1. **Little of the nutrients is lost**, because the food is not in contact with the water, so the vitamins and minerals do not dissolve and are not thrown away.
2. **The food is easily digested**, so it is suitable for babies, sick people and old people.
3. **No fat is needed and the food does not burn or stick**, and the flavour, colour and shape of the food are kept. It is also economical, because several foods can be cooked together over one source of heat.
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
i) Mention five (5) functions of proteins in the body.

(5 marks)

ii) Outline five (5) ways of slowing down food decay

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Five functions of proteins in the body (1 mark each)**

1. **Growth** - proteins build the new cells and tissues of a growing child, an adolescent or a pregnant woman.
2. **Repair and replacement** of worn-out or damaged cells and tissues, for example after a wound or an illness.
3. **Making enzymes and hormones**, which control digestion and other body processes.
4. **Making antibodies**, which protect the body against infection.
5. **Supplying energy** when there is not enough carbohydrate and fat (1 g of protein gives about 17 kJ).

**(ii) Five ways of slowing down food decay (1 mark each)**

Food decays because bacteria, moulds and yeasts grow in it and because enzymes in the food act on it. Decay is slowed down by:

1. **Refrigeration** - the cold temperature slows the growth of micro-organisms.
2. **Freezing** - at very low temperatures micro-organisms stop growing.
3. **Drying** - removing the water that micro-organisms need (for example dried fish, beans and pepper).
4. **Salting or smoking** - salt draws water out of the food, and smoke dries it and gives a protective coating (for example smoked fish and salted meat).
5. **Canning or bottling** - the food is heated in a sealed container, which destroys micro-organisms and keeps new ones out.

(Other correct answers: adding sugar, as in jam; pickling in vinegar; adding permitted preservatives; storing food covered in a clean, cool, airtight container.)
